description:
Three near-identical hex implementations live in the crate:

1. pkix-lint/src/lib.rs:175-196 — cert_sha256_hex serializer/deserializer uses char::from_digit and u8::from_str_radix on string slices.
2. pkix-lint/src/oscal/emit.rs:819-839 — hex() and hex_digit() free functions, pure index arithmetic.
3. pkix-lint/src/oscal/parse.rs:866-892 — hex_decode() and nibble() free functions, bytes-indexed.

Plus a fourth re-implementation in emit.rs's own test module (1581-1605) because hex_decode in parse.rs is private.

The lib.rs serde shape is unique (and broken — see PKIX-7f92.1) but the other three are byte-identical. Pulling them into a single private mod hex { fn encode/fn decode/fn nibble } would let the broken serde codec use the same primitives as the other two and avoid the panic bug entirely.

Suggested rewrite: introduce pkix-lint/src/hex.rs (or a sub-mod of oscal) exposing pub(crate) fn encode(&[u8]) -> String and pub(crate) fn decode(&str) -> Option<Vec<u8>>, then port every call site. The serde codec in lib.rs becomes:

  let bytes = hex::decode(&hex).ok_or_else(|| de::Error::custom('non-hex'))?;
  if bytes.len() != 32 { return Err(de::Error::invalid_length(bytes.len(), &'32-byte sha256')) }
  let mut out = [0u8; 32]; out.copy_from_slice(&bytes); Ok(Some(out))

Both shorter and panic-free.

Filed as elegance not correctness because the broken serializer is filed separately. This is the refactor that closes both.
title: Hex encoding/decoding duplicated in three modules
